title: Enrich regression alert payload + post to incident-bot webhook
author: Rafael Mendes
description:
Motivation: The regression detector is firing useful signals, but the current alert payload is too thin to support fast oncall triage (folks immediately ask: what dashboard panel should I open, what runtime build just changed, and is this aligned with a deploy). This PR enriches the payload emitted by perf-canary and adds a best-effort integration that posts a structured message to incident-bot (#eng-oncall) when a page/ticket is created.

What’s in this PR: Add alert payload enrichment fields: dashboard links (per model/region/slice), runbook link, and drill-down query parameters; last deploy context: deploy annotation timestamp, runtime_version, runtime_build, git_sha, and region; runtime build diff: when we have a prior build for the same slice, include a compare link (build A -> build B) and the commit range when available; baseline context: baseline strategy (rolling median), baseline window, effective sample size, and suppression flags; detector context: which metric regressed (p95_latency_ms, tokens_per_sec), regression ratio/absolute deltas, and minimum-sample gate evaluation.

Incident-bot integration: Adds a small webhook client that POSTs the enriched payload to incident-bot (configurable endpoint) and formats a compact message with links + key dimensions. The webhook is best-effort and non-blocking: failures are logged and counted, but do not prevent paging/ticket creation. Includes request signing using HMAC (shared secret) and retry with exponential backoff (bounded).

Notes on safety/cardinality: No new metric labels are introduced here; this change only enriches the alert payload and incident-bot message content. The dashboard URLs are constructed from existing dimensions already present in alerts (model, region, gpu_sku, runtime_build, scheduler_mode).

Testing: Unit tests cover URL construction (Grafana links), payload serialization stability, webhook signing, and retry behavior. Added an integration-ish test that runs the detector on a canned regression sample and snapshots the incident-bot payload.

Rollout plan: Deploy perf-canary with INCIDENT_BOT_WEBHOOK_URL set in us-east first. We’ll keep posting in “ticket-only” mode for 24h (no PagerDuty page) while verifying message formatting and link correctness, then enable paging for confirmed regressions.

Screenshots/Example output: Example incident-bot message (rendered): "Perf regression: llama-3.1-70b-instruct (us-east / H100 / scheduler=pinned) p95 +18% vs baseline; tokens/sec -9%. Dashboard: ... Runbook: ... Last deploy: runtime_build=runtime-2026.02.09.1 sha=7c1e9b2 Compare: ...".

Follow-ups: We should standardize the compare link format with Release Engineering (deploy annotations doc) and consider adding an optional ‘recent PRs touching runtime scheduling’ hint once runtime build->PR mapping is reliable.

Refs: ENG-2853 (incident-bot annotations), ENG-2848 (alert routing), ENG-2846 (detector logic).
commits: detector: add EnrichedAlertContext and populate deploy/baseline fields
grafana: centralize dashboard url builder w/ slice-aware params
incident-bot: add webhook client + signing + retry/backoff
alerting: attach runtime build compare link when prior build exists
tests: snapshot incident-bot payload + url builder unit tests
docs: env vars + local test instructions for webhook
review_conversation: Sean Gallagher (review): Payload looks good. Two requests: (1) make incident-bot posting non-blocking (do not delay PagerDuty path) and (2) include a clear dedup key in the message (model/region/gpu/runtime_build + metric). Also please add a note on what happens during maintenance window suppression (so oncall isn’t confused by missing posts).

Rafael Mendes (author): Done. Webhook is now in a goroutine with a short context timeout; failures increment incidentbot_post_failures_total and are logged w/ request id. Added dedup_key to payload + message and documented suppression behavior in docs/alert-payload.md.

Logan Wright (review): +1 overall. Concern: the dashboard URL builder is doing string concatenation with labels. Please ensure we URL-encode model names and scheduler_mode values. Also, can we cap the payload size (some fields like compare ranges could grow)?

Rafael Mendes (author): Good catch. Added proper url.QueryEscape for all query params + a max length guard on compare_commit_range (truncate + include ‘…’). Payload JSON is also capped at 32KB before posting; if exceeded we drop optional fields (compare range first) and log a warning.

Felix Schneider (review): The Grafana links are nearly right, but the panel targets expect region to be ‘us-east-1’ not ‘us-east’ for the dashboard variable. Can we translate to the dashboard’s canonical naming? Also please include the dashboard uid as a config value instead of hardcoding.

Rafael Mendes (author): Updated: added RegionToDashboardVar() mapping (us-east -> us-east-1, eu-west -> eu-west-1) and made GRAFANA_DASHBOARD_UID_PERF_CANARY configurable (default kept for now). Added tests for mapping.

Tomáš Novák (review): Please add a small ‘what to do first’ ordering in the incident-bot message. Something like: 1) open dashboard, 2) check last deploy annotation, 3) check suppression flag. Even 1 line helps people at 3am.
Rafael Mendes (author): Added a short ‘Triage: dashboard -> deploy annotation -> runbook’ line at the top of the message and ensured runbook link is always present when posting.
Sean Gallagher (follow-up): Looks good now. Approved once we confirm retry/backoff won’t spam incident-bot on prolonged outage.

Rafael Mendes (author): Retry is bounded (max 3 attempts, jittered exponential, total < 10s) and we short-circuit on 4xx. Added a circuit-breaker-ish counter to stop posting for 5m if we see 20 consecutive failures.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Rafael Mendes. Squash commit: 3f8b0f7. Release note: perf-canary alerts now include dashboard/runbook/deploy context and will post structured messages to incident-bot when configured.
